profile.summary: DiffMS generates candidate molecular structures from a tandem mass spectrum (de novo structure elucidation). It takes an MS/MS spectrum and the molecule's chemical formula, encodes the spectrum with a formula transformer, and uses a discrete graph diffusion model to build molecular graphs with the right heavy atoms. It outputs a set of sampled candidate structures.

summary_quotes.text: One formulation of the structure elucidation task is the conditional de novo generation of molecular structure given a mass spectrum.
The encoder utilizes a transformer architecture and models mass spectra domain knowledge such as peak formulae and neutral losses,
and the decoder is a discrete graph diffusion model restricted by the heavy-atom composition of a known chemical formula.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The encoder is the MIST formula transformer, which embeds spectrum peaks labelled with formulas and neutral losses. The decoder is a discrete graph diffusion model adapted from DiGress: it denoises an adjacency matrix over a fixed set of heavy atoms taken from the known formula, and hydrogens are placed implicitly. The decoder is pretrained on 2.8M fingerprint-molecule pairs (2048-bit Morgan fingerprints, radius 2) from DSSTox, HMDB, COCONUT and MOSES; the encoder is pretrained on the finetuning data (NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym); then the whole model is finetuned with the denoising cross-entropy loss.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Pretrained end-to-end models and decoders are on Zenodo record 23542112 (published 2026-10-21, MIT, files diffms_checkpoints.tar.gz and msg_preprocessed.tar.gz). MIST encoder checkpoints are on a separate Zenodo record, in four variants (CANOPUS or MassSpecGym, with or without synthetic training spectra), with training code in coleygroup/MIST. The MassSpecGym in the Wild paper reports that the MIST attention code as first published in the MIST and DiffMS codebases mishandled padding in batched inputs, and that a commonly reused MIST checkpoint from DiffMS could not be reproduced. A result should name the checkpoint files, the MIST encoder variant and the code commit.

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: MassSpecGym in the Wild (an existing source on this record) lists DiffMS in its updated MassSpecGym de novo leaderboard and also uses it for generative retrieval. It shows that changing metric settings on identical DiffMS predictions changes the scores, and recommends keeping metric code consistent with the MassSpecGym reference implementation.

facts.value: Conditional generative model: formula-restricted encoder-decoder for de novo molecule generation from mass spectra.

quotes.text: we present DiffMS, a formularestricted encoder-decoder generative network

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: MIST formula transformer encoder plus a discrete graph diffusion decoder (adapted from DiGress) over heavy atoms.

quotes.text: we adopt the formula transformer from MIST
the decoder is a discrete graph diffusion model

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An MS/MS spectrum with peak formula annotations and the target's chemical formula (inferable from MS1 with tools such as SIRIUS or MIST-CF).

quotes.text: restricted by the heavy-atom composition of a known chemical formula.
Formulae can be inferred from high-resolution MS1 data and isotopic traces with sufficient accuracy using tools like SIRIUS

facts.value: Decoder pretraining: 2.8M fingerprint-molecule pairs from DSSTox, HMDB, COCONUT and MOSES. Encoder pretraining and finetuning: NPLIB1 (CANOPUS) or MassSpecGym.

quotes.text: 2.8M fingerprint-molecule pairs sampled from DSSTox (CCTE, 2019), HMDB (Wishart et al., 2021), COCONUT (Sorokina et al., 2021), and MOSES (Polykovskiy et al., 2020) datasets.
You will also need to set the dataset in [config.yaml](configs/config.yaml) to 'msg' for MassSpecGym or 'canopus' for NPLIB1.

strengths.text: Decoder pretraining uses fingerprint-molecule pairs, which are plentiful compared with spectrum-structure pairs; the authors report performance scaling with pretraining set size.

quotes.text: we pretrain the diffusion decoder with fingerprint-structure pairs, which are available in virtually infinite quantities
show consistent performance scaling with increasing pretraining dataset size.

strengths.text: Relatively light: all experiments ran on 12 GB NVIDIA 2080 Ti GPUs (the authors' report).

quotes.text: all experiments were run on NVIDIA 2080ti GPUs with 12 GB of memory.

limitations.text: MassSpecGym in the Wild found a batched-padding bug in the MIST encoder code as first published in DiffMS and an unreproducible MIST checkpoint reused downstream; results that depend on that checkpoint need care.

quotes.text: Padding tokens therefore receive a finite +1 attention offset rather than being excluded from the softmax, affecting both training and inference with padded batches.

limitations.text: Scores are sensitive to metric settings; the de novo leaderboard values differ by implementation.
